What is this?

Write the front end. Watch it run.

Forkbench is an in-browser code playground. You type HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into three editor panes, and a sandboxed preview re-runs your code live as you go. There's a captured console for your console.log() calls and runtime errors, draggable layout, autosave, shareable links, and one-click export. The entire thing runs client-side — open index.html and it just works.

What's inside

Everything is hand-built vanilla JavaScript — no editor library, no framework, no build step.

A real editor

A textarea with a syntax-highlighted overlay, line numbers, tab-to-indent, bracket and quote auto-pairing, and a current-line highlight — written from scratch.

Live sandboxed preview

Your three sources are assembled into an iframe with srcdoc and a sandbox attribute, debounced so it re-runs smoothly as you type.

Captured console

A tiny shim inside the preview forwards console.log/warn/error and uncaught errors to a console panel over postMessage.

Rearrangeable layout

Drag the splitters, switch between side-by-side and stacked, and toggle individual panes on or off. Keyboard-resizable too.

Autosave & sharing

Your pen autosaves to localStorage. Share encodes the whole pen into the URL hash; export downloads a single combined HTML file.

Starter templates

Six ready-to-run pens — a CSS aurora, a canvas sketch, an SVG clock, a to-do app and more — one click from the gallery.

How a run actually happens

Four steps, all in the browser, every time you (auto-)run.

You edit a pane

An input event updates the pen object and, with auto-run on, schedules a debounced run 600 ms later.

The document is assembled

HTML, a <style> from your CSS, the console shim, and your JS are stitched into one document string.

The iframe re-runs

Assigning iframe.srcdoc tears down and recreates the preview document, cleanly restarting timers and animation loops.

Output flows back

The shim posts each console call to the parent window, which renders it in the console panel with level-based styling and filters.

Keyboard shortcuts

The editor is fully keyboard-driven.

Ctrl / ⌘ + EnterRun the pen now (also clears the console)
Ctrl / ⌘ + SForce-save the pen to local storage
Ctrl / ⌘ + Shift + KClear the console
Ctrl / ⌘ + 1 / 2 / 3Focus the HTML / CSS / JS pane
Tab / Shift + TabIndent / dedent (works on a selection too)

Common questions

Where is my code stored?

Only in your own browser. The current pen is autosaved to localStorage, and shared links carry the code in the URL itself. Nothing is sent to a server — there isn't one.

Is the preview safe?

Your JavaScript runs inside a sandboxed <iframe>. It can script, show modals, and submit forms within itself, but it is isolated from the Forkbench app shell. The only channel between them is the console postMessage bridge.

Can I use an external library?

Add a <script src="…"> tag in the HTML pane and it will load inside the preview, just like a normal page — assuming you're online. The editor itself ships with zero dependencies.

What does Export give me?

A single self-contained .html file with your CSS inlined in a <style> and your JS in a <script> — open it anywhere, no Forkbench required.
